cases.question: How is this website itself tested?
cases.answer: Every control has a stable data-testid and is covered by Playwright end-to-end tests on desktop and mobile Chromium, plus visual regression screenshots, axe accessibility scans, and CSP and privacy checks. GitHub Actions runs lint, type checks and the full suite on every change, only a green run can deploy, and each deploy publishes its own test results. Visitors can also run live checks in their own browser.

cases.question: How does a change to this site get from a request to the live site?
cases.answer: A Claude Code workflow takes it through five gates. Plan: a read-only planner agent writes acceptance criteria, each with a named Playwright test. Build: tests come first, then the smallest change that passes, with hooks as guard rails. Test: npm run verify must pass. Verify: a second agent with a fresh context marks each criterion pass or fail. Deploy: the agent commits and stops, Harry pushes, CI reruns every check, and a smoke check confirms the live commit.

judge.reason: Each stage matches the portfolio text and it stays within the word limit, with a small loss because the clipped, label-led style reads like notes and “confirms the live commit” compresses what the smoke check does.
